title: Asynchronous paths have a dead-letter queue
whatToLookFor: New SQS queues, Lambda event-source mappings, SNS subscriptions, or Step Functions that lack a DLQ or `onFailure` destination. Without a DLQ, failed messages are silently dropped after retries exhaust.

title: Retry policy is explicit and idempotent
whatToLookFor: Lambda handlers or downstream calls that retry on failure without idempotency keys, conditional writes, or de-duplication. SQS `maxReceiveCount` left at the default when the consumer's idempotency story is unclear. SNS subscriptions without a redrive policy.

title: Timeouts are set explicitly and match the upstream contract
whatToLookFor: Lambdas that default to the platform timeout when the upstream caller (API Gateway, Step Functions) has its own shorter limit, downstream HTTP clients without a connect or read timeout, or SQS `visibilityTimeout` shorter than the longest possible processing time of the consuming Lambda.

title: Throttling and back-pressure protect downstream resources
whatToLookFor: Lambdas without `reservedConcurrentExecutions` when they call rate-limited downstream services, API Gateway stages without throttling settings, SNS-to-SQS fan-outs that can swamp the downstream Lambda's concurrency.

title: Alarms cover the failure modes the change introduces
whatToLookFor: New Lambda functions without `Errors` or `Throttles` alarms, new SQS queues without `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` or DLQ-depth alarms, new API Gateway routes without 5XX-rate alarms. A new failure mode without an alarm is invisible.

title: Recovery is automated where stakes are low and documented where they are high
whatToLookFor: Reactive paths (DLQ drain, retry replay, traffic shift) that require manual intervention without a runbook entry, or critical recovery steps that are scripted but not also documented for the on-call. Stateful resources without backup or point-in-time-recovery configured.

title: Multi-AZ posture matches the resource type and the workload SLO
whatToLookFor: Single-AZ deployments of resources that support multi-AZ (RDS, ElastiCache, EFS, NAT gateways) when the SLO documented in AGENTS.md or the runbook calls for higher availability. Lambdas in a VPC pinned to a single subnet.

title: Circuit-breaker patterns protect against cascading failures
whatToLookFor: Long-running synchronous chains where a slow or failing dependency would block all upstream callers, missing circuit-breaker libraries on outbound HTTP from Lambdas that fan out widely, or absence of provisioned concurrency on a critical path that warm-starts under load.

title: Graceful degradation: the change defines what 'partial' looks like
whatToLookFor: New features that either fully succeed or fully fail, with no documented partial-success path; downstream lookups whose absence crashes the request when a sensible default would let the path complete; cache misses treated as fatal.

title: Dependency failures are isolated, not propagated
whatToLookFor: A new external dependency (third-party API, peer service, shared SQS queue) introduced without bulkheading, without a fallback path, or without a feature flag that lets operators disable it under load.

title: Capacity and quotas are checked against the change's growth profile
whatToLookFor: Lambda concurrency adds that approach the account's concurrent-execution quota, new SQS queues with high throughput that approach the FIFO-throughput limit, or fan-out widths that risk the SNS subscriptions-per-topic limit. A change that works in preview but not at scale.

title: Stateful resources have backup or point-in-time recovery configured
whatToLookFor: New DynamoDB tables without `pointInTimeRecovery`, RDS instances without automated backups, or S3 buckets holding non-derivable data without versioning. Recoverability should be designed in at creation, not bolted on later.

title: Change-deployment strategy fits the blast radius
whatToLookFor: All-at-once Lambda alias updates on critical paths where canary or linear deployments would be safer, lack of pre/post-traffic hooks on a function whose failure would be hard to detect immediately, or stack-level changes that recreate stateful resources.
